title: Chapter 117 — The Coaching Craft: Observation, Feedback & The One-to-One
intro: Floor observation, the feedback formula, and the one-to-one architecture.

sections.title: The Coaching Framework
sections.content: Observe: watch the rep with a customer without intervening. Note what they did well and where they lost momentum. Ask: after the interaction, 'How do you think that went?' Let them self-assess first. Reinforce: start with what they did right — specific praise. Develop: one area to improve, not five. One. Practice: role-play the specific skill.

sections.title: The Weekly One-on-One
sections.content:
Fifteen minutes. Every week. Non-negotiable.

'How are you feeling about this week?' Check the human, not just the numbers. 'What was your best interaction this week?' Reinforce positive behaviour. 'What was your toughest interaction?' Coach on it. 'What do you need from me?' Remove obstacles. 'Here is your focus for next week: one specific thing.'

Not five things. One thing. The rep who improves one skill per week has improved 50 skills by the end of the year.

sections.title: Coaching Mistakes
sections.content:
Telling instead of asking. 'You should have...' is less effective than 'What would you do differently?' Coaching only when things go wrong — reinforce good habits too. Coaching in front of customers — always in private. Using your own selling style as the template — different reps sell differently, coach to their strengths. Ignoring top performers — they need coaching too, just different coaching.

Never lead with punishment. Lead with curiosity. 'I noticed your close rate dropped. Help me understand what is happening.' Then coach the specific skill that moves the specific number.
